paper.title_en: Can Entangled Parallel Universes (EPU) ameliorate the cosmic tensions?
paper.abstract_en: We propose the Entangled Parallel Universes (EPU) framework, in which late-time cosmic acceleration emerges from a geometric coupling between our universe and a partner manifold characterized by a Euclidean-signature line element. We emphasize from the outset that the term “entangled” is used here in a purely classical, geometric-causal sense – denoting a kinematic coupling between two manifolds enforced by a null constraint – and carries no connection to quantum-mechanical entanglement. In this construction, our universe is embedded within the host manifold and connected to it through null-like channels that enforce photon-speed propagation. While the Euclidean geometry of the host space admits superluminal motion, the connecting structure preserves causal consistency by dynamically enforcing the speed-of-light constraint. This enforcement generates a geometric tension within the channels, leading to their gradual shortening over cosmic time. The shortening mechanism produces a dual dynamical effect: expansion of our universe and contraction of the host manifold. The associated geometric tension acts as an effective dark-energy source of purely gravitational origin. Although the underlying construction is classical and introduces no exotic matter or energy-condition violation, the resulting effective equation of state is intrinsically phantom-like. Remarkably, the framework naturally yields the Chevallier–Polarski–Linder (CPL) functional form of the dark-energy equation of state with fixed coefficients (<math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3740"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3757"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math>) determined from first principles, rather than treating <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3779"><msub><mrow><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3789"><msub><mrow><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub></math> as free fitting parameters as in the phenomenological CPL parametrization. The model contains no cosmological constant and does not require a scalar-field potential. Confronted with Pantheon+, DESI BAO and RSD, Union 3.1, DES, R22 local measurements, and CMB constraints, the EPU model provides a good fit to current data. It reduces the Hubble tension to <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3799"><mrow><mn>0.39</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math> and the <math altimg="si769.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3807"><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub></math> tension to approximately <math altimg="si7.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3818"><mrow><mn>1.7</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math>, positioning EPU as a viable phenomenological geometric alternative to <math altimg="si8.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3826"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math>CDM in which cosmic acceleration arises from causal protection and inter-manifold connectivity.
